engine.title: The multibagger screen qualified nobody for four weeks
engine.body: Corrects what this entry said on 2026-08-27. It read ‘the scan is running on schedule’ and blamed the fixed list on cadence. The ledger says otherwise: the last multibagger row is 2026-08-01, while magic, magicmagic and ai_longterm — the same Saturday job, the same slot — all logged 2026-08-22. Twenty-six days, three Saturdays, nothing written.
engine.note: The screen is not broken. Run on 2026-08-27 it took 11 candidates and rejected 10 for R:R below 2.0 — CHENNPETRO 1.29, FLUOROCHEM 1.07, GLAXO 0.59, which needs a 63% win rate merely to break even. The defect was that a week qualifying nobody wrote nothing at all, so the page served the 1 August list as though it were current. The attempt is recorded either way now. The gate is NOT loosened: publishing a 0.59 R:R to keep the section busy is the exact trade this screen exists to refuse, and an empty week is a real result.

engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Calculation: The LPDO Rule
chess.body: LPDO = Loose Pieces Drop Off. Before every move, scan the board: which of my pieces are undefended? Which of my opponent's pieces are undefended? Undefended pieces are targets for tactics. A simple habit: after finding your move, ask 'does this leave anything undefended?' This alone prevents most blunders.

wisdom.title: The Gratitude Practise
wisdom.body: Every morning, before checking your phone: name 3 specific things you're grateful for. Not 'health and family' — that's lazy. Something specific: 'my daughter smiled when she saw me yesterday,' 'I understood a balance sheet faster than last year,' 'KL at 26°C.' Specificity trains the brain to notice abundance.

book.author: Jim Collins
book.lesson: Collins expected great companies to be led by charismatic visionary CEOs. He found the opposite. Every good-to-great company had a Level 5 leader — someone who combined fierce professional will with personal humility. They were ambitious for the company, not themselves. When things went well, they looked out the window and gave credit to others. When things went wrong, they looked in the mirror and took responsibility. They were more like Lincoln than Patton — quietly determined rather than loudly inspiring.
book.key_quote: The most effective leaders are often the least visible. Ego is the enemy of great leadership.
book.action: Next time something goes well on your team, actively give someone else the credit. Notice how it feels and what it does to team morale.
crux: Good is the enemy of great. Most organisations never become great because they become good enough.
Level 5 Leadership: extreme personal humility combined with intense professional will.
First Who, Then What. Get the right people on the bus before setting direction.
Confront the brutal facts while never losing faith — the Stockdale Paradox.
The Hedgehog Concept: the intersection of what you're deeply passionate about, what you can be best in the world at, and what drives your economics.
One economic denominator — profit per X — clarifies the entire business.
A culture of discipline, not a tyrant imposing discipline.
Technology accelerates momentum; it never creates it.
The Flywheel: relentless pushing in a consistent direction until momentum compounds.
The Doom Loop is the opposite — new programmes, new directions, no accumulation.
Great companies had no miracle moment. Transformation looked dramatic only from outside.
Stop-doing lists matter more than to-do lists.
Compensation gets the right people on the bus; it does not motivate the wrong ones.
learnings: Who beats what. Wrong people make the right strategy fail.
Facing bad news early is a competitive advantage.
Momentum accumulates from consistent direction, not from bursts of intensity.
Greatness is mostly a series of unglamorous, consistent decisions.
examples: Walgreens beat the market 15x from 1975–2000 by fixating on profit per customer visit — one metric, relentlessly.
Darwin Smith at Kimberly-Clark sold the paper mills — the company's historic core — to enter consumer paper against P&G. Shareholder returns beat the market 4x.
Nucor's flywheel: mini-mill technology → lower cost → market share → more mills. Same push for decades.
adapt: Hedgehog: CA precision + FP&A + building with AI. That intersection is narrower and stronger than 'finance content'.
Economic denominator for Codex: profit per customer, not downloads.
Brutal fact: 1H signals have no measurable edge. Faith: the daily equity engine does. Hold both.
Stop-doing list beats the roadmap. Deleting three TradeFlow pages was the flywheel push.

minimalism.title: Buy Once, Cry Once
minimalism.body: Minimalism is not cheapness. One well-made pair of shoes at 4x the price that lasts 10x as long is both cheaper and lighter. Fewer, better beats more, adequate.
minimalism.action: List three things you have replaced more than twice. Buy the good version once.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: Never Discuss What Someone Earns
etiquette.body: Not theirs, not yours, not a third party's. It creates comparison where none existed and it always travels. Especially in the Gulf, where packages vary enormously by nationality and contract.
etiquette.action: Deflect the next compensation question with warmth, not information.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: Desire Is The Contract
stillness.body: Every want you accept is a contract to be unhappy until it is satisfied. Most were installed by advertising, not chosen. Audit the source before signing.
stillness.action: Name one want. Trace where it came from. Decide if it is yours.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Second-Order Thinking
model.body: And then what? Most bad decisions are first-order correct. Price caps look like they help until supply disappears. Ask 'and then what?' three times before committing.
model.action: Take today's main decision three steps forward.
model.label: Mental Model

arabic.meaning: Please, go ahead / here you are
arabic.use: Offering a seat, food, or the floor in a meeting. tafaddali to a woman.
arabic.label: Arabic

drill.title: Speak For 60 Seconds, No Filler
drill.body: Record yourself explaining something for a minute with no 'um', 'like', or 'basically'. Silence between sentences reads as authority. Filler reads as uncertainty.
drill.action: Record 60 seconds. Count the filler words. Repeat until zero.
drill.label: Drill

health.title: Protein: 1.6g Per Kg, Minimum
health.body: At 75kg that is 120g daily — far above most intakes. Protein is the one macro where the deficiency is common and the consequence is muscle you cannot easily get back.
health.action: Compute your target. Hit it for one day and see how hard it actually is.
health.label: Health

quote.quote: One child, one teacher, one book, one pen can change the world.

lesson.lesson: He who fears death will never do anything worthy of a living man.

case.title: Apple: The Return of Steve Jobs (1997)
case.story: Apple was 90 days from bankruptcy. Jobs cut product lines from 350 to 10. Result: Apple went from $3B revenue to $350B+ in 15 years.
case.lesson: Focus ruthlessly. Saying no to 1,000 things is the secret to innovation. Complexity kills companies.

fpna.title: Zero-Based Budgeting
fpna.body: Start every budget from ₹0. Justify every line. Cuts 15–30% bloat in most orgs.

cfo.title: The CA→FC→CFO Timeline
cfo.body: CA qualified → 2-3 years Big 4/audit → Senior FP&A → Finance Manager → Financial Controller (5-8 years post-qualification) → CFO (10-15 years). Dubai compresses this by 2-3 years if you hit the right company at the right growth stage.

money_hack.title: The 50-30-20 Rule
money_hack.body: 50% needs · 30% wants · 20% savings. Automate the 20% on salary day.

dubai.title: Who actually hires FP&A in the UAE
dubai.body: Four pools, in order of volume: government-linked groups (ADNOC, DEWA, Etihad), retail and F&B conglomerates (MAF, Landmark, Alshaya), logistics and ports (DP World, Aramex), and Big 4 advisory. Retail hires the most and pays the least. Government-linked pays the most and moves slowest.
dubai.targets: Best ratio of pay to speed: logistics and healthcare groups.
dubai.action: Pick one pool. Applying across all four with one CV is why nothing lands.

desk.productivity: Batch similar tasks. Answer all messages in one sitting.

father.title: Narrate what you are doing
father.do: Talk through ordinary actions out loud while she watches — 'I am pouring the water, now it is warm.'
father.why: At 7 months she is mapping sound to meaning long before she can speak. Volume of directed speech is the single best-evidenced predictor of later vocabulary. Passive audio does not count; it has to be you, to her.

father.title: Read the same book again
father.do: Read one board book daily, the same one, for a week. Point at the same picture each time.
father.why: Repetition is how infants build prediction. The boredom is yours, not hers — she is learning that symbols hold steady meaning.

life_wisdom.teaching: Every claim is true only under stated conditions. Jain logic prefixes assertions with 'in some respect' to keep the conditions visible.
life_wisdom.apply: Attach the assumption to the forecast, out loud: 'growth is 12% — in the respect that the two new stores open in Q3.' Half of forecasting disputes are actually undeclared conditions.

life_wisdom.teaching: The first noble truth is not 'life is suffering' but that conditioned things do not stay satisfying. The promotion satisfies briefly, then resets.
life_wisdom.apply: Before chasing the next milestone, name honestly what the last one actually changed and for how long. Then decide if you still want it.

vocab.meaning: The ability to produce the intended result.
vocab.example: We have no evidence on the efficacy of that promotion.
vocab.note: Not the same as efficiency. Efficacy is 'does it work', efficiency is 'at what cost'.

vocab.example: Only AED 3M of that is incremental revenue.
vocab.note: The single most important word in investment appraisal. Everything hinges on the baseline.

speaking.title: Cut the runway
speaking.drill: Record yourself answering 'what do you do?' in 30 seconds. Count how many words come before your first concrete noun. Redo it until the answer starts with the thing itself.
speaking.why: Most people spend 8 seconds warming up. Senior listeners have decided what they think of you by then.

interview_tech.q: You acquire 80% of a subsidiary. Walk me through the consolidation mechanics.
interview_tech.a: Recognise 100% of the subsidiary's assets and liabilities at fair value, not 80% — control, not ownership, drives consolidation. The 20% you do not own becomes non-controlling interest, shown within equity. Goodwill is consideration transferred plus NCI measured either at fair value (full goodwill) or at its share of net assets (partial goodwill) — an accounting policy choice that changes the goodwill number materially. Eliminate all intragroup balances, transactions and unrealised profit in stock. Post-acquisition profit splits between parent and NCI by ownership.

interview_tech.q: What is shrinkage, what causes it, and what is an acceptable level?
interview_tech.a: Shrinkage is the gap between book inventory and counted inventory — theft (external and internal), administrative error, damage and supplier short-delivery. Fashion retail typically runs 1–2% of sales; grocery higher. The important split is internal versus external, because the remedies differ entirely: internal is a controls and rostering problem, external is layout, tagging and security. Any store more than 100bps above the estate average is a process failure, not bad luck — investigate the receiving dock first.

interview_soft.q: The board pushes back hard on your numbers in front of everyone. What do you do?
interview_soft.a: Do not defend and do not fold. Separate the challenge into fact and judgement. If they have spotted a factual error, concede immediately and precisely — 'you are right, that is the restated base, I will recirculate by Thursday.' Credibility survives errors; it does not survive defensiveness. If it is a judgement call, state your assumption, the sensitivity, and offer the alternative case. Never argue methodology in the room; take it offline with the one director who raised it.

interview_soft.q: An employee asks you to approve an expense that is within policy but clearly wrong. What now?
interview_soft.a: They are testing whether you hide behind rules. Policy is a floor, not a ceiling. Approve or reject on the substance, explain the reasoning to the person directly, and then fix the policy so the next person is not in the same position. If it involves a senior person, the answer does not change — that is precisely when it counts. Say plainly that you would escalate to the audit committee if pressured to approve something you believe is wrong.
interview_soft.who: Any group with a code of conduct
